discussion: New at WWDC '25, the @Animatable macro generates the animatableData plumbing from a type's stored numeric properties — custom shapes and modifiers animate without hand-written getters and setters; @AnimatableIgnored opts a property out.
name: @Animatable
summary: Macro that synthesizes animatableData for a type.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:_:store:)
children.summary: Backs a non-optional Bool, Int, Double, String, URL, or Data property with a UserDefaults key, using the inline default until something writes to it.

children.name: init(_:store:)
children.summary: Declares an optional-typed preference that reads as nil until a value has been stored, so no default is required.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:_:store:) where Value: RawRepresentable
children.summary: Stores an enum whose raw value is a String or Int, letting a Picker bind straight to a typed preference.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:_:store:) — TableColumnCustomization
children.summary: Persists a Table's user-arranged column order, widths, and visibility under a key; macOS 14 and iOS 17 or later.

code:
@AppStorage("fontSize") private var fontSize = 14.0

Slider(value: $fontSize, in: 10...24)
discussion: @AppStorage reads and writes a UserDefaults key while behaving like @State — the view updates when the value changes from anywhere, including Settings panes. Best for small preferences, not documents.
name: @AppStorage
summary: State persisted automatically in UserDefaults.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:)
children.summary: Wraps an @Observable instance the view already holds; declaring it as a local inside body is the idiom when the object came from @Environment.

children.name: init(_:)
children.summary: Builds a Bindable value explicitly, so bindings can be pulled from any observable reference without a wrapper declaration.

children.code:
@Bindable var book: Book

TextField("Title", text: $book.title)
Stepper("Pages: \(book.pageCount)", value: $book.pageCount, in: 1...2000)
Slider(value: $book.rating, in: 0...5)
children.name: subscript(dynamicMember:)
children.summary: The $ syntax resolves through a dynamic-member subscript that turns a writable key path on the object into a Binding to that property.

discussion: @Bindable bridges the gap the macro left: wrap an @Observable reference with it — as a property or a local in body — and the $ syntax yields bindings to its properties for use with controls.
name: @Bindable
summary: Creates bindings into an @Observable object.

children.name: init(get:set:)
children.summary: Assembles a binding from a getter and a setter closure, which is how you adapt or invert a value on its way to a control.

children.name: constant(_:)
children.summary: A binding pinned to one value that silently drops writes, ideal for previews and read-only demonstrations of two-way controls.

children.name: init(_:)
children.summary: A failable initializer that unwraps a Binding<Value?> into a Binding<Value>, returning nil while the underlying value is absent.

children.name: animation(_:)
children.summary: Returns a copy of the binding whose writes run inside the given animation, so a control's change animates without withAnimation at the call site.

discussion: @Binding lets a child view mutate its parent's state without owning it — the $ prefix on a @State property produces one. It is the backbone of every two-way control, from TextField to Toggle.
name: @Binding
summary: A read-write reference to state owned elsewhere.

children.name: @Entry in ContainerValues
children.summary: Declares a per-subview value that a child sets with containerValue and a container reads back through containerValues while iterating subviews; iOS 18 and macOS 15 or later.

children.name: @Entry in FocusedValues
children.summary: Stands in for a hand-written FocusedValueKey; the property is optional because focus may be nowhere relevant at all.

children.name: @Entry in Transaction
children.summary: Adds a custom flag to Transaction that animation code can inspect, set through the key-path form of withTransaction.

discussion: The @Entry macro (WWDC '24) replaces the EnvironmentKey boilerplate: annotate a var in an EnvironmentValues extension with a default value, and it becomes a fully usable custom environment entry. It works for transaction, container, and focused values too.
name: @Entry
summary: Declares a custom environment value in one line.

children.name: init(_:) — EnvironmentValues key path
children.summary: Reads a system-provided value by key path into EnvironmentValues, whether a plain value like locale or an action such as dismiss.

children.name: init(_:) — Observable type
children.summary: Looks up an @Observable object by its type, matching whatever an ancestor injected with the environment(_:) modifier; iOS 17 and macOS 14 or later.

children.name: init(_:) — optional Observable
children.summary: Declaring the property as optional makes a missing injection read as nil instead of crashing at runtime.

discussion: @Environment pulls system values — color scheme, locale, dismiss — or your own @Observable models injected with .environment out of the context. Values flow down the tree, and any ancestor can override them for its subtree.
name: @Environment
summary: Reads a value the surrounding hierarchy provides.

discussion: @EnvironmentObject pulls a shared ObservableObject placed with environmentObject from any descendant — crashing at runtime if nobody injected it. New code on current targets shares @Observable models through plain @Environment instead.
name: @EnvironmentObject
summary: Reads an ObservableObject injected upstream.

children.name: init(sortDescriptors:predicate:animation:)
children.summary: The modern form: Swift SortDescriptors plus an optional NSPredicate, with an animation applied whenever the result set changes.

children.name: init(fetchRequest:animation:)
children.summary: Hands the wrapper a fully configured NSFetchRequest, the only route to fetch limits, batching, and relationship prefetching.

children.name: init(entity:sortDescriptors:predicate:animation:)
children.summary: The original form that names the entity description explicitly and takes Foundation NSSortDescriptors.

children.name: projectedValue (Configuration)
children.summary: The $ form is a binding to the request's configuration, so a Table or picker can rewrite the sort descriptors and predicate while the view is live.

discussion: @FetchRequest runs a fetch against the managedObjectContext in the environment and re-renders the view as objects change, with sort descriptors and predicates in the declaration. Requires import CoreData.
name: @FetchRequest
summary: Live Core Data query results as a view property.

children.name: init(_:) — FocusedValues key path
children.summary: Reads whichever value the focused view published under that FocusedValues key, or nil when nothing relevant has focus.

children.name: init(_:) — Observable type
children.summary: Looks up a focused @Observable object by type rather than key path, paired with the focusedValue(_:) overload that takes the object directly; iOS 17 and macOS 14 or later.

children.name: FocusedValueKey
children.summary: The pre-@Entry way to define a focused value: a key type declaring the value's type plus a computed accessor on FocusedValues.

discussion: Focused values flow from whatever currently has focus to interested observers — the mechanism menu commands use to act on 'the focused document'. Publish with focusedValue, read with @FocusedValue.
name: @FocusedValue
summary: Reads a value published by the focused view.

children.name: init() — Bool
children.summary: A Boolean focus state tracks a single field, pairing with the focused(_:) modifier that takes no equals value.

children.name: init() — Optional<Hashable>
children.summary: An optional Hashable value tracks focus across many fields, and any Hashable works as the tag, not only an enum case.

children.name: projectedValue (FocusState.Binding)
children.summary: The $ form is a FocusState.Binding that a parent can hand to a child view so the child moves focus the parent owns.

discussion: @FocusState pairs with the focused modifier: a Boolean for one field, or a hashable enum to manage focus across a form. Setting the property moves focus; nil (or false) dismisses the keyboard.
name: @FocusState
summary: Tracks and drives which view has keyboard focus.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:)
children.summary: Sets the resting value the property returns to whenever the gesture ends or is cancelled.

children.code:
@GestureState(resetTransaction: Transaction(animation: .bouncy))
private var offset = CGSize.zero

Circle()
    .offset(offset)
    .gesture(DragGesture().updating($offset) { value, state, _ in
        state = value.translation
    })
children.name: init(wrappedValue:resetTransaction:)
children.summary: Supplies the transaction used for the snap-back, which is how you pick the animation the reset plays.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:reset:)
children.summary: Runs a closure with the final value and an inout Transaction when the gesture ends, so the reset animation can depend on where the gesture finished.

children.code:
@GestureState private var pressedID: Item.ID?

Row(item)
    .scaleEffect(pressedID == item.id ? 0.95 : 1)
    .gesture(LongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.2)
        .updating($pressedID) { _, state, _ in state = item.id })
children.name: init()
children.summary: For optional value types the state starts at nil with no explicit default and returns to nil after each gesture.

discussion: @GestureState stores in-flight gesture data — a drag translation, a pinch scale — and snaps back to its initial value the moment the gesture finishes, with the reset animating automatically.
name: @GestureState
summary: Transient state that resets when a gesture ends.

discussion: @Namespace mints a unique namespace tying together matchedGeometryEffect pairs, zoom transition sources, and focus scopes within one view hierarchy.
name: @Namespace
summary: An identifier space for matched geometry and focus.

children.name: init(_:)
children.summary: Passes the delegate class as a metatype; SwiftUI instantiates it and installs it as the application delegate before the scene body runs.

children.name: init()
children.summary: Infers the delegate class from the property's declared type, so the .self argument can be omitted.

children.name: projectedValue — ObservableObject delegate
children.summary: When the delegate also conforms to ObservableObject, $appDelegate yields bindings to its published properties and the instance is placed in the environment automatically.

discussion: Declared on the App struct, this wrapper instantiates your NSApplicationDelegate so lifecycle callbacks SwiftUI doesn't surface — Sparkle updaters, dock menu APIs, legacy integrations — still have a home.
name: @NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor
summary: Attaches an AppKit app delegate to a SwiftUI app.

children.name: @ObservationIgnored
children.summary: Excludes a stored property from change tracking, which you want for internal plumbing such as caches or in-flight tasks.

children.name: withObservationTracking(_:onChange:)
children.summary: The raw mechanism behind SwiftUI's tracking: runs the closure, records which properties it read, and calls onChange the first time any of them mutates.

children.name: Observations(_:)
children.summary: Introduced with Swift 6.2 for the 26 releases, an AsyncSequence that yields a new value whenever the tracked properties read inside the closure change.

discussion: The @Observable macro (WWDC '23) replaces ObservableObject for new code: no @Published, and views re-render only when properties they actually read change. Store instances in @State, share them via .environment, and bind with @Bindable.
name: @Observable
summary: Macro that makes a class's properties observable.

discussion: @ObservedObject re-renders the view when the object's @Published properties change, but does not keep the object alive — the parent must own it (typically via @StateObject). Superseded by plain properties on @Observable models.
name: @ObservedObject
summary: Subscribes to an ObservableObject owned elsewhere.

discussion: The @Previewable macro (WWDC '24) lets a #Preview declare @State and other dynamic properties inline — interactive previews without wrapping everything in a throwaway container view.
name: @Previewable
summary: Allows live state directly inside a #Preview.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:)
children.summary: Wraps a stored property on an ObservableObject; a private(set) keeps mutation inside the class while views still react.

children.code:
model.$query
    .debounce(for: .milliseconds(300), scheduler: RunLoop.main)
    .removeDuplicates()
    .sink { [weak model] text in model?.search(text) }
    .store(in: &cancellables)
children.name: projectedValue (Published.Publisher)
children.summary: Reading $property from outside the class gives a Combine publisher that emits each new value just before it is stored.

discussion: @Published fires objectWillChange before every mutation, which is what @StateObject and @ObservedObject listen for. It belongs to Combine's ObservableObject world; the @Observable macro tracks properties without it.
name: @Published
summary: Marks an ObservableObject property as change-emitting.

children.name: init(filter:sort:order:animation:)
children.summary: Filters with a #Predicate and orders by a single Comparable key path, animating changes to the result set.

children.name: init(filter:sort:animation:)
children.summary: Takes an array of SortDescriptors for multi-key ordering; assigning to the underscored storage lets a view derive its query from init arguments.

children.name: init(_:animation:)
children.summary: Accepts a prebuilt FetchDescriptor, the route to fetch limits, offsets, and relationship prefetching that the convenience forms do not expose.

discussion: @Query is SwiftData's answer to @FetchRequest: declarative filtering and sorting over @Model types from the modelContext, updating the view as the store changes. Requires import SwiftData.
name: @Query
summary: Live SwiftData query results as a view property.

discussion: @ScaledMetric multiplies your base value by the user's text-size setting, optionally relative to a specific text style — keeping icons and spacing proportional to enlarged text.
name: @ScaledMetric
summary: A number that scales with Dynamic Type.

code:
@SceneStorage("selectedTab") private var tab = "home"

TabView(selection: $tab) { … }
discussion: @SceneStorage saves lightweight UI state — selected tab, scroll target, draft text — scoped to each window, so two windows restore independently. The system owns the storage; treat it as best-effort.
name: @SceneStorage
summary: Per-scene state restored across app launches.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:)
children.summary: The everyday form: the inline default becomes the initial value when the view's identity is first created, and later re-initializations are ignored.

children.name: init()
children.summary: Optional-typed state begins as nil with no assignment at all, the usual shape for selection and sheet-driving values.

children.name: projectedValue
children.summary: The $ prefix produces a Binding<Value>, and key-path chaining on that binding reaches individual fields of a struct.

children.name: @State holding an @Observable object
children.summary: Since iOS 17 and macOS 14 the wrapper also owns a reference-type model, creating it once per view identity and re-rendering only for properties body actually reads.

discussion: @State moves a value out of the transient view struct into storage SwiftUI manages, re-rendering the view when it changes. Keep it private and pass it down as bindings; since WWDC '23 it also holds @Observable model objects.
name: @State
summary: View-owned storage that survives re-rendering.

children.name: init(wrappedValue:)
children.summary: The argument is an escaping autoclosure evaluated once per view identity, so even an explicit assignment in a view's init does not rebuild the object on re-render.

children.name: projectedValue (ObservedObject.Wrapper)
children.summary: The $ form yields bindings to the object's published properties through dynamic member lookup.

discussion: @StateObject instantiates an ObservableObject once per view identity and keeps it alive across re-renders — the legacy counterpart of @State + @Observable. In new code targeting current OSes, prefer the @Observable macro.
name: @StateObject
summary: Owns an ObservableObject for the view's lifetime.

children.name: init(_:)
children.summary: Passes the delegate class as a metatype; SwiftUI creates the instance and wires it up as the shared application's delegate.

children.name: init()
children.summary: Infers the delegate class from the property's declared type, dropping the explicit .self argument.

children.name: projectedValue — ObservableObject delegate
children.summary: An ObservableObject delegate is injected into the environment automatically, and $appDelegate exposes bindings to its published properties.

discussion: The iOS counterpart: hosts a UIApplicationDelegate for push-notification registration, third-party SDK hooks, and other callbacks the SwiftUI lifecycle doesn't expose directly.
name: @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor
summary: Attaches a UIKit app delegate to a SwiftUI app.
